episodes.171955: An early morning storm produced a marine thunderstorm wind gust.
episodes.171975: A broken line of thunderstorms developed Friday afternoon along a cold front that was moving southeast across west-central Wisconsin. Ample instability and marginal wind shear allowed for one storm to produced 1.5 inch hail east of Deer Park, Wisconsin, in the far northeast corner of St. Croix County. Most of the other storms that late afternoon and early evening weren't as strong and may have produced some hail and gusty winds, but no other reports were received.
episodes.172043: Slow-moving showers and thunderstorms along the Volusia County coast produced a couple of waterspouts that remained over the Atlantic waters before dissipating.
episodes.173031: Afternoon sea breeze thunderstorms produce gusty winds over the coastal waters around Tampa Bay.
episodes.173032: Afternoon thunderstorms produce wind damage at two mobile communities between Bradenton and Bayshore Gardens in Manatee County.
episodes.173248: Under a classic setup for storm motion from the Mogollon Rim to the Valley (Rim-to-Valley), with the monsoon 500mb high positioned over Nevada, a multicell storm cluster descended out of the White Mountains, through Gila County, and into the lower deserts of Maricopa and Pinal Counties in the early overnight hours of the 1st. Moisture levels were near average for the time of year, but steep mid level lapse rates over the high terrain (7-8 C/km) and modest shear (Sfc-6km around 20-25 kts) was sufficient to support the development of an organized multicell storm cluster. The environment was also supportive of strong downbursts, with DCAPE up around 1000-1500 J/kg. A single ordinary storm also developed in the Queen Creek/San Tan Valley area a couple hours before the multicell cluster moved into the lower deserts, and produced a damaging downburst. Strong winds leading to a dust storm was eventually generated by the multicell cluster once it moved into Maricopa and Pinal Counties.
episodes.173487: A broad area of showers and storms produced localized flooding.
episodes.173491: Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a slow moving upper level disturbance that tracked eastward across the southern Plains into the lower and middle Mississippi Valley from the 2nd to the early morning of the 3rd. Several reports of flash flooding were received south of Highway 60 from Aurora and Cassville, and eastward toward Ava. Rainfall accumulations for the 24-hour period ending at 1 AM on 9/3/22 showed a large area of one to two inches along and east of a line from Joplin to Versailles, with greater than two inches along and south of a line from Monett to Mountain Grove. A few locations in Douglas County received over 5 inches of rain.
episodes.173726: Isolated thunderstorm gust in Alamosa from a passing thunderstorm.
episodes.173845: Scattered strong summer storms resulted in gusty winds in excess of 34 knots across portions of the coastal waters.
episodes.173875: The pattern was unsettled during the first week of September. On the 2nd, a front wobbled across Arkansas, and triggered scattered showers and thunderstorms across the northern counties. Two to three inches of rain dumped at a few locations. Twenty four hour amounts through 600 am CST on the 3rd included 2.56 inches at Mountain Home (Baxter County), 2.25 inches at Jordan (Baxter County), and 2.10 inches at Clarksville (Johnson County). Trees and limbs were knocked down south of Nimrod Lake.
episodes.174029: Deep monsoon moisture and light shear in the atmosphere brought strong to severe storms over northern Arizona with local flash flooding.
episodes.174074: Slow moving thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon of the 1st across northern Oklahoma, with isolated flash flooding reported. Later additional thunderstorms developed in western Oklahoma with reports of severe wind gusts.
episodes.174129: A cold front moving across the Northland produced showers and storms across the region during the evening hours of the 2nd. While most of the storms remained below severe limits, one storm did produce 1 inch diameter hail near the town of Winter in Sawyer County.
episodes.174134: Isolated to scattered thunderstorms developed over portions of Northwest Kansas and extreme Southwest Nebraska, moving south. As the storms moved across Northwest Kansas, wind gusts up to 70 mph caused damage to a Cottonwood tree and small tents in eastern Graham County. As storms moved over eastern Wichita County, up to penny sized hail was observed.
episodes.174136: Scattered thunderstorms developed over extreme Southwest Nebraska, moving south across Red Willow County. One storm produced quarter sized hail near the town of Bartley, Nebraska.
episodes.174319: A man drowned in Lake Mohave near Cottonwood Cove. Witnesses reported that the man was swimming, and breezy winds prevented him from making it back to his boat.
episodes.174320: A weak push of monsoon moisture plus ongoing record heat fueled scattered thunderstorms over Mohave County. A few produced severe weather and flash flooding.
episodes.174436: An isolated thunderstorm developed near a weak stationary front along the Beaufort County coast. A lightning strike occurred on the beach, injuring one person.
episodes.174438: An isolated thunderstorm developed near a weak stationary front along the Beaufort County coast. The storm produced a waterspout about 2 miles offshore that lasted for nearly 15 minutes.
episodes.174463: A couple of isolated storms produced a couple of reports of damaging winds on September 1st, 2022.  One occurred in southeast Kansas and the other occurred in central Kansas.
episodes.174527: Thunderstorms produced torrential rainfall which produced flash flooding in San Angelo.
episodes.174572: A weak mid level boundary progressed through the southern CWA with sufficient enough instability and shear to go along with the 30-35 temperature dew point spread to produced isolated severe thunderstorms. With weak mid level winds, storms moved slowly south to southwest seeing some decent rain amounts as well.

events.narrative: Several large tree limbs were knocked down across town.
KSN TV reported, RV campers were rolled over by damaging winds.
A roof was blown off a building.
Power poles were blown down in this area.
There were several large 12 to 18 inch diameter tree limbs blown down in southwest Dodge City.
Farm Road 1232 was flooded at a low water area.

A bus barn at Poston Butte High School had two 3X70 foot pieces of sheet metal roofing peeled off in a downburst. A stack of wooden pallets was reportedly tossed 150 feet and there was at least minor damage to other equipment and supplies. A light pole, rusted near the base, also toppled over at the high school. Wind speeds estimated around 55-60 mph and timing based on radar. No injuries were reported.
Approximately 5-6 trees, at 20 to 30 feet tall, were toppled on Johnson Ranch Boulevard. Wind speeds estimated around 55-60 mph and timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.

Two large trees (20-24 inch diameter trunks) were uprooted and each fell through concrete block walls and onto a couple homes in the Johnson Ranch community. The extent of the damage to the homes was unknown. There were also several street signs reportedly ripped from their posts or were twisted/mangled. Winds were estimated around 55-60 mph and timing was based on radar. No injuries were reported.

Beaufort County Emergency Management reported that a woman was struck by lightning on the beach at Hilton Head near Palmetto Dunes. The woman was struck on the shoulder with distinct entrance and exit wounds. The woman stopped breathing but was successfully revived with CPR. Three people standing approximately 15 feet away from the victim observed their hair stand on end before the strike and were knocked to the ground by the jolt, but uninjured.
